blocks.text: AI Security continuously scans your cloud resources against the policies enabled in your cloud accounts to identify vulnerabilities and generate issues. When a policy violation is detected, AI Security generates issues and sends notifications to recipients to take action and prevent any potential breaches.

An issue is the outcome of a policy evaluation done on a resource type (e.g., S3 bucket, database). For example, if a security policy is enabled to detect any publicly exposed S3 bucket containing sensitive data, and there are 5 such S3 buckets in your cloud storage, AI Security generates 5 issues.
Issues are categorized by severity level to help you prioritize them and take action in a timely manner.
Issues provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: View and manage issue notifications for any security policy violations detected in the cloud accounts.
Notify recipients to take action and prevent any potential breaches.
Stay informed about critical security events.

blocks.text: On the Issues View page (AI Infrastructure > Issues > Issues View), you can see the following generated issues:

blocks.item: Apply filters to view specific data.
By default, issues with an open status are displayed.
Add additional filters.
Search for specific data in the searchable column.
Modify the table and its columns.
View the list of issues generated for policy violations. For each issue, you can view:
Issue ID: The unique identifier for the issue. Click to view additional details.
Resource Name: The name of the resource.
Policy Name: The policy title.
Policy Category: The threat category (Public Exposure, Data Loss, etc.) to which the policy belongs.
Resource Type: The type of data store (AWS EC2 instance, AWS S3 bucket, etc.).
Resource ID: The unique identifier for the resource.
Risk Level: The risk level (Critical, High, Medium, or Low) of the issue.

The risk level of an issue is calculated as the average of the policy severity and the resource impact. For example, if the policy severity is Critical and the resource impact is Medium, then the issue risk level is High.
Issue Status: The status (Open, Closed, Resolved, and Snoozed) of the issue.
Cloud Account: The unique identifier of the cloud account (AWS, Azure, GCP, Snowflake, and On-Premises) in which the resource is located.
Created At: The date and time the issue was generated.
Updated At: The date and time the issue was last updated.
Select one or multiple issues to resolve, snooze, unsnooze, or reset them.
Actions provide the option to Resolve or Snooze the issue. To learn more, see Resolve an issue and Snooze an issue.
